title: After an Eight-Year Journey, BepiColombo Slips Into Orbit Around Mercury

content:
After an eight-year cruise across the solar system, the European-Japanese BepiColombo spacecraft has entered orbit around Mercury — the first spacecraft to visit the planet in more than a decade.

The spacecraft was captured into orbit on Saturday, Nov. 21, the European Space Agency announced, according to The Associated Press.

BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft ever to visit Mercury. NASA's Mariner 10 flew by the planet in the mid-1970s, and NASA's Messenger orbited Mercury from 2011 to 2015.

The mission is a joint effort by the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), costing about $2 billion. It launched in 2018.

The journey covered more than 6 billion miles, using one Earth flyby, two Venus flybys and six Mercury flybys for gravity assists to slow the spacecraft down enough to be captured by the planet's gravity. The transfer module that powered the cruise was shed in September 2026.

BepiColombo actually carries two linked orbiters: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mio. The two will separate on Dec. 9-10, 2026, and then study Mercury from different altitudes, making simultaneous measurements of the planet's interior, magnetic field, craters and volcanic plains.

The initial orbit is elliptical, about 590 by 11,640 kilometers. The Mercury Planetary Orbiter will descend to its final science orbit, 400 to 1,500 kilometers above the surface, by March 2027, with science operations starting in April 2027.

Mercury is a punishing place to work. Its surface can exceed 800 degrees Fahrenheit, and the mission is planned to run at least one Earth year — four Mercury years.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones of ESA said the mission will allow "unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time," with new data expected from spring 2027.

The mission is named for Italian mathematician Giuseppe "Bepi" Colombo, who worked on the Mariner 10 mission. The exact orbit-insertion time and further details on spacecraft health beyond confirmation of capture had not yet been made public when the AP reported the arrival.

Sources: The Associated Press, Nov. 23, 2026; European Space Agency; Nature.
